Data efficiency

Dataset condensation for efficient learning

A compact synthetic training set preserved 82.5 percent evaluation accuracy while using only four percent of the original data.

Case study

Keep the information, not every example.

Data efficiencySynthetic dataPyTorchEvaluation

The problem

Large training sets increase storage, iteration time, and compute cost. Dataset condensation asks whether a small set of optimized examples can carry much of the information needed to train a useful model.

The approach

The project generated compact synthetic samples and evaluated how well a model trained on them transferred to the full test distribution. The codebase includes the report and plotting workflow so the accuracy–compression tradeoff can be reproduced.

Accuracy retained as data shrinkssynthetic set: 4% of data

Result

Using four percent of the original data, the condensed set supported 82.5 percent test accuracy. The result makes the tradeoff concrete: a 25× reduction in examples while retaining much of the decision boundary.

Takeaway

Efficient learning is not only about smaller models. Better-chosen data can reduce the cost of training, experimentation, and deployment pipelines.
